retatrutide.elimination_after_last_dose: NOT ESTABLISHED. No label or SmPC exists (investigational). The only human elimination data come from a 4-participant antidoping study in which retatrutide remained DETECTABLE in plasma (not necessarily active or at therapeutic levels) at 1344 h (56 days) after the first of two 2 mg subcutaneous doses; the authors state: 'The extended plasma detection window, approximately 56 days after the first dose, supports plasma-based testing...'. Detection is not the same as elimination and no elimination time is defined.

retatrutide.notes: RETATRUTIDE IS INVESTIGATIONAL: it is not approved by the FDA, EMA or NMPA, has no prescribing information, and no brand name (brand_names is therefore an empty list, not a missing value). What is NOT established: absolute/subcutaneous bioavailability (null), time to steady state (null), accumulation ratio (null), apparent clearance (null) and volume of distribution (null) - none of these is reported in any source located. half_life_hours = 144 is a unit conversion of 'approximately 6 days'; the figure appears in the INTRODUCTION of the 2026 Rapid Communications in Mass Spectrometry paper, attributed to Coskun et al. Cell Metab 2022 (doi:10.1016/j.cmet.2022.07.013), whose full text was paywalled and could NOT be checked directly - so the 6-day value is a secondary quotation, not a verified primary measurement. The tmax value comes from a 4-participant non-regulatory study in which participants SELF-ADMINISTERED product obtained from a non-pharmaceutical source ('Retatrutide (LY3437943; purity >= 95%) was obtained from Ozel Form (Istanbul, Turkey)'), with no pharmacokinetic sampling between 168 h and 336 h; treat tmax_hours = 24 as the LOWER bound of a very imprecise 24-48 h observation. The 56-day figure is a plasma DETECTION window, not an elimination time.

tirzepatide.trial: SURMOUNT (obesity/overweight): pooled 2 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials = SURMOUNT-1 + SURMOUNT-2, Zepbound label section 6.1, Table 2. Values shown are the ZEPBOUND 15 mg arm (N=941) vs placebo (N=958).
tirzepatide.notes: Full dose-response in the same table (placebo / 5 mg / 10 mg / 15 mg): nausea 8/25/29/28%; diarrhoea 8/19/21/23%; vomiting 2/8/11/13%; constipation 5/17/14/11%. Any GI adverse reaction: placebo 30% vs 56% at every Zepbound dose. GI-related discontinuation: placebo 0.5%, 5 mg 1.9%, 10 mg 3.3%, 15 mg 4.3%. For type 2 diabetes (SURPASS programme), the Mounjaro label Table 1 pooled placebo-controlled adult T2D trials give (placebo / 5 mg / 10 mg / 15 mg): nausea 4/12/15/18%; diarrhoea 9/12/13/17%; vomiting 2/5/5/9%; constipation 1/6/6/7%. Nausea is therefore markedly more common in the obesity trials than in the T2D trials at the same doses.

semaglutide.trial: Wegovy 2.4 mg (obesity/overweight): pooled 3 randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials, Wegovy label section 6.1, Table 3. N=2,116 (Wegovy 2.4 mg) vs N=1,261 (placebo), up to 68 weeks.
semaglutide.notes: These are the Wegovy 2.4 mg (weight-management) figures. The corresponding Ozempic 1 mg T2D figures are much lower - the Ozempic label reports any gastrointestinal adverse reaction in 30.8% at 1 mg and 34% at 2 mg. Semaglutide 2.4 mg has the highest reported nausea incidence of the drugs in this set (44%), higher than tirzepatide 15 mg (28%) in SURMOUNT.

gi_side_effects.onset_and_attenuation: REGULATORY WORDING (strongest evidence). Tirzepatide: the Zepbound label states 'The majority of nausea, vomiting, and/or diarrhea events occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time.' The Mounjaro label states 'The majority of reports of nausea, vomiting, and/or diarrhea occurred during dose escalation and decreased over time.' Neither the Wegovy nor the Ozempic label contains an equivalent 'decreased over time' sentence (searched; absent). PEAK TIMING: a 2026 peer-reviewed narrative review of GI adverse effects of GLP-1 RAs and dual GIP/GLP-1 RAs states 'Symptoms peak within the 1st week of initiation or dose escalation and decrease with continued use' and that the events are 'typically during initiation and dose escalation' (Garg et al., Nutr Clin Pract 2026, doi:10.1002/ncp.70180). ATTENUATION / TOLERANCE: a 2026 quantitative analysis of dose-escalation regimens in T2D (Nauck et al., Diabetes Obes Metab 2026, doi:10.1111/dom.70613) found that after completing the recommended dose-escalation regimens, '2-5-fold higher doses of semaglutide and tirzepatide can be tolerated', and that tolerance for nausea/vomiting was significantly associated with a longer dose-escalation period and a greater number of escalation steps; the same analysis found NO such tolerance development for dulaglutide, exenatide once weekly, albiglutide, liraglutide, exenatide twice daily or lixisenatide. MITIGATION: the same 2026 review states 'Slow dose escalation, which is advancing no faster than monthly, is the single most robust mitigation strategy'. NOT FOUND: no source located gives a quantitative statement of the DURATION of an individual nausea episode, and none gives a peak time in hours after a single injection (e.g. '24-48 h post-dose'); both are explicitly unverified. CAVEAT: the two 2026 papers are peer-reviewed reviews/analyses, not primary trial data; the label statements are regulatory primary wording but are qualitative, not quantitative.

body_composition.notes: TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES ARE OFTEN CONFLATED - both are given here explicitly. (a) 'percent of TOTAL WEIGHT LOST that was lean mass': verified for tirzepatide as approximately 25% (SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy, n=160, published 2025 in Diabetes Obes Metab, doi:10.1111/dom.16275 - note: an earlier widely-circulated DOI 10.1111/dom.15391 for this substudy could NOT be verified and is not used). (b) 'percent CHANGE IN LEAN MASS from baseline': tirzepatide -10.9% (pooled doses) vs placebo -2.6% in the same substudy; semaglutide -9.7% vs placebo in the STEP 1 DEXA substudy. For SEMAGLUTIDE, quantity (a) could NOT be verified from the STEP 1 DEXA substudy - that abstract reports only the -9.7% lean-mass change, the -15.0% weight change and a +3.0 percentage-point increase in the lean-mass PROPORTION of body mass. semaglutide_lean_mass_pct is therefore null rather than estimated; do not compute it by dividing -9.7 by -15.0, as those are percentages of different baselines. Two secondary/aggregate sources exist but were deliberately NOT used as the primary number because they are not drug-specific primary trial data: a 2026 meta-analysis of 7 RCTs (n=821, doi:10.1038/s41366-026-02118-y) and a 2026 review of 40 DXA reports (mean fat-free-mass loss 29.1%, SD 19.0%, doi:10.1002/oby.70212). PROTEIN: the numeric field holds 1.2 g/kg/day because the schema requires a single number and 1.2 is the LOWER BOUND of the advisory's explicitly stated 1.2-1.6 g/kg body weight/day range for active weight reduction; it is NOT a midpoint or a point estimate. The same advisory also gives 1.2-2.0 g/kg ADJUSTED body weight/day and 1.5 g/kg fat-free mass/day, and states there is NO consensus on which body-weight basis to use. The STEP 1 body-composition analysis is a conference abstract (J Endocr Soc 2021;5(Suppl 1):A16, PMCID PMC8089287) - the only open-access version located; no full peer-reviewed paper for it was found.
